source_bins.C01: Recognize a new useful art of likeness from nature, named improntare; the previous treatment of coloring is declared sufficient.
source_bins.C02: Select the human model, young/woman/old; beard and hair are difficult, and the beard is to be shaved.
source_bins.C03: Oil the face with fragrant rose oil using a substantial squirrel-hair brush; cover the head with cap or hood.
source_bins.C04: Prepare a handbreadth-wide cloth, shoulder-to-shoulder length; sew it around the cap from one ear to the other.
source_bins.C05: Place cotton in both ears; sew and route the same cloth at collar, shoulders and front buttons, returning to its beginning.
source_bins.C06: Lay the model on a carpet on table/board. Prepare an iron ring 1–2 fingers wide, with saw-like teeth, 2–3 fingers longer than the face.
source_bins.C07: An assistant holds the ring clear of the face. Attach the free cloth edge to its teeth; retain about two fingers or slightly less clearance around the face for the expected cast.
source_bins.C08: State that the casting material is to be poured into that prepared enclosure; la impronta is the prospective made object.
source_bins.C09: Have a goldsmith make two lightweight brass or silver tubes, trumpet-like wider above, nearly a handbreadth long and a finger thick.
source_bins.C10: The lower ends fit the nostrils without expanding them; small holes perforate the upper halves; bind the tubes together at the bottom respecting the space between nostrils.
source_bins.C11: Place the model supine; put those tubes into the nostrils and have the model hold them.
source_bins.C12: Use freshly prepared, cooked, sifted Bolognese or Volterran gypsum and warm water in a basin; mix quickly because it sets quickly, neither too fluid nor too stiff.
source_bins.C13: Use a glass to pour some of this compound evenly around the face, covering eyes last; eyes and mouth shut naturally, as in sleep.
source_bins.C14: Fill to one finger above the nose and let it set a little.
source_bins.C15: For a high-status model, use warm rose water; for others, warm spring/well/river water suffices. This is a conditional material substitution, not a new unmarked action.
source_bins.C16: Once dry, cut away the sewn cloth with one of three stated tools and remove the tubes gently.
source_bins.C17: Raise/remove the model while holding/supporting the compound and gently free the face from the mask/form; the exact bodily-motion wording is textually corrupt in the edition.
source_bins.C18: Put away and preserve that first mask/form.
source_bins.C19: Surround the same form with a baby swaddling band projecting two fingers above its edge.
source_bins.C20: Oil the cavity carefully with any chosen oil and a thick squirrel-hair brush, lest the work come to nothing.
source_bins.C21: Prepare further gypsum by the earlier method; optionally improve it by adding crushed-brick powder. This preparation call does not assert reuse of the first hardened physical gypsum.
source_bins.C22: Pour this further gypsum into the earlier form using glass and bowl while holding it on a bench.
source_bins.C23: Tap the bench gently with the other hand so the fill reaches everywhere like wax in a seal, without bubbles/blisters.
source_bins.C24: Rest the filled form half a day, at most a day.
source_bins.C25: Carefully break the outer shell, explicitly the first form, while preserving the nose and everything else of the new representation.
source_bins.C26: Optional earlier preparation: before filling, saw the exterior in several places to weaken the first form, without cutting through; this enables small hammer blows to break it after filling.
source_bins.C27: State the resulting effigy/likeness/impronta of the model.
source_bins.C28: Claim that this form/first form permits casting the said impronta in copper, metal, bronze, gold, silver, lead or any desired metal; the exact antecedent after destructive release is not resolved.
source_bins.C29: Require competent masters who understand melting and casting; the passage does not give a complete foundry workflow.

uncertainties.detail: MODEL supports the compound is an explicit working parse, compatible with1859but not a unique resolution of corrupt1821wording; no reader certainty asserted.
Purpose avoid work failure follows context and1859guasto, while1821questo niente is transmitted corruptly; explicit content assumption.
FIRST_FORM reference is retained as a designation, without asserting a unique physical antecedent or present availability after BREAK1.
Carpet on table/board is the selected support layering; treating carpet/table/board as three alternatives is another reading of the punctuation, not settled by the source.

identity_policy: MODEL_SELF=MODEL; different batches/portions/molds/results are not silently identified. MASK1 is the first outer shell; CAST2 survives. No actual breath-function claim from editorial headings.
epistemic_policy: All records preserve discourse modality; directives and conditional/possible claims are not observed executions. Compound scalar/relational values such as ONE_FINGER are explicit finite semantic values, not a claim to morphemic indivisibility. C01–C29 are provenance bins, not code terminals.

entity_definitions.WORKER: instructional addressee, distinct role from author/speaker and sitter
entity_definitions.BATCH1: prepared mixed first gypsum batch; BATCH1_GYPSUM is its ingredient, not the batch itself
entity_definitions.POURED1: unspecified portion of BATCH1 used around the face
entity_definitions.MASK1: first hardened form resulting from POURED1; later outer shell
entity_definitions.BATCH2: new mixed gypsum batch made by reference to MIX1 method
entity_definitions.CAST2: analytic identifier for the second formed representation protected during BREAK1 and subsequently called effigy/likeness/imprint; not an additional source-named object
entity_definitions.SPEAKER: source discourse speaker; not automatically the worker
entity_definitions.FIRST_FORM: source designation in ambiguous later metal possibility; physical antecedent deliberately not equated by this fact writer
